## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Apply the 2ℓk-vertex kernel in polynomial time for fixed ℓ.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_{\ell}(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O_{\ell}(k^{\ell+1}+k)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{\ell+1,3\}$ |

## Derivation

1. For each connected vertex set S of size ℓ+1 in the kernel, add $\bigvee_{v\in S}x_v$. Every connected component with more than ℓ vertices contains such a set.

2. Consequently, hitting all these sets is equivalent to having no remaining component larger than ℓ. Add the linear cardinality encoding.

3. The total number of variables is O_ℓ(k). The width is constant and the number of clauses is polynomial for fixed ℓ, giving the general-density bound.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- This entry does not claim an FPT bound for the combined parameter (k,ℓ); the cited preprocessing takes n^{O(ℓ)} time.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
